newsitem.title: PERU: Rescuers recover 44 bodies from Aeroperu crash.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers recover 44 bodies from Aeroperu crash.

text.p: Peruvian airline Aeroperu said on Friday rescuers had recovered the bodies of another 17 victims from its Boeing 757 that crashed into the Pacific ocean a month ago, bringing to 44 the number of bodies found.

The airline said a robot belonging to the U.S firm contracted for the rescue, Oceaneering Technologies, located and brought up the 17 bodies on Thursday. They were taken to the morgue of Lima's neighbouring port of Callao while rescue operations to find the remaining 26 bodies continued.
The nine crew members and 61 passengers from 11 countries were travelling on Oct. 2 on Flight 603 from Lima to Santiago when the plane crashed into the sea northwest of Lima.
Transport Minister Elsa Carrera said this week results of an analysis of the "black box" flight recorders by U.S. aviation experts would take about two months.

Peru's government has pinned the blame for the accident on technical faults that made the computers aboard the plane "go crazy," leaving the pilot, Eric Schreiber, without instruments as he struggled to return to Lima after takeoff.
But investigators from Aeroperu, Boeing, engine maker Pratt & Whitney and the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have so far reserved judgment.
The 70 dead came from Chile, Peru, Mexico, Ecuador, the United States, Italy, Great Britain, New Zealand, Spain, Colombia and Venezuela.

The accident, one of the worst in Peru's aviation history, came seven months after a Boeing 737 belonging to local Faucett airline crashed and killed all 123 people on board near Peru's second city, Arequipa. Since 1967, a total of 601 people have been killed in air crashes in Peru.
